I read the current default calibration of garnet (set f81c45da-6e73-4b5d-a0fe-72c75635fade) and ranked every CZ pair by its IRB CZ fidelity. The best 3-qubit chain is QB11-QB12-QB7, with QB12 in the middle. The pair QB12-QB11 has fidelity 0.998693 and QB12-QB7 has 0.998016. The product is 0.996712. No other chain beats it. The next best chain was QB16-QB11-QB12, at about 0.9947.

I built a GHZ circuit directly on those physical qubits. It puts a Hadamard on QB12, then does a CNOT from QB12 to each end qubit, built as H, CZ, H. Only the QB12-QB11 and QB12-QB7 CZ pairs are used. I measured all 3 qubits, with bit order QB11, QB12, QB7. I ran it on garnet:mock with 200 shots. The job ID is 01a16040-776a-71f7-bea0-dc2f5816ce3b. The counts were 000: 39, 011: 54, 100: 59, 111: 48.

The mock backend does not simulate the circuit, so these counts are not real GHZ results. A real GHZ state would give only 000 and 111, about half each. The mock also returns 011 and 100, so this run does not test the circuit. On real hardware, the CZ fidelities above show how much noise to expect. A chain of high-fidelity pairs should keep the 000 and 111 peaks strong. The principle is that a quantum computer's qubits and links differ in quality, so choosing the best connected qubits improves the result.
